resources.string: Full-screen per-frame noise overlay that raises the noise floor of the display\'s electromagnetic emission.
The app needs the \"Display over other apps\" permission to draw the noise layer.
Android 13+ requires notification permission to show the foreground-service status notification.
Higher values mask more but make the screen harder to read. This is the real trade-off; there is no free lunch.
Independent random value per pixel per frame, flat spectrum.
Energy concentrated in high horizontal spatial frequencies: adjacent pixels along a row are anti-correlated, which is where the pixel-clock emission lives.
Horizontal HF noise plus several sub-patterns mixed within one frame for extra temporal decorrelation.

• Windows flagged FLAG_SECURE (banking, DRM video, password screens) are rendered by the system so that this overlay does NOT appear above them. Those screens are not protected.
 • Noise is re-randomised every frame because a static pattern averages out as 1/√N over N captured frames. Even so, averaging still reduces the effect; this is a noise-floor raise, not a guarantee.
 • No effectiveness has been measured with real RF equipment on your device. Treat this as a prototype and as a complement to hardware shielding, never a replacement.
 • Continuous full-screen GPU rendering costs battery.
 • Android 12+ caps the opacity of click-through overlays at about 80 %; above that the system would block touches to other apps. The slider's top end is therefore the system cap.
 • While the overlay runs, some permission dialogs and Settings screens refuse taps ("screen overlay detected"). Stop the overlay to use them.
